column5: Description
A member can ask a question and get a correct answer from the WinCS FAQ.
The assistant is tested, does not invent answers and handles harmful input safely.
The assistant is easy to use, measured with SUS before and after improvements.
Velocity, burndown and cycle time are tracked in Power BI; docs live in Confluence.

column4: Set up repository and dev environment
column5:
As the developer, I want a GitHub repo with a README and venv setup so that anyone can run the project.

Acceptance criteria:
Repo is public; README has setup steps; app runs locally from a fresh clone.

As a WinCS member, I want the assistant to use real society information so that answers are accurate.

Acceptance criteria:
Committee has reviewed and approved the knowledge_base files; every SAMPLE banner removed.

As the developer, I want the FAQ split into sections so that the bot can find the right one.

Acceptance criteria:
Each '## ' heading becomes one section; unit test passes.

column4: Retrieve relevant FAQ sections for a question
column5:
As a member, I want my question matched to the right FAQ section so that I get a relevant answer.

Acceptance criteria:
Top-4 retrieval contains the right section for 4 sample questions (unit tests).

As a member, I want a short answer in plain language so that I do not have to read the whole FAQ.

Acceptance criteria:
Answers use only the retrieved context; model and effort configurable by env var.

As a member, I want a simple chat window so that I can ask questions without technical skills.

Acceptance criteria:
Streamlit chat shows history, a spinner while loading, and a Clear chat button.

As a member, I want to see which FAQ section an answer came from so that I can trust it.

Acceptance criteria:
Each answered message has a Sources expander listing section names.

column4: Say 'I don't know' instead of guessing
column5:
As a member, I want the bot to admit when it doesn't know so that I am not misled.

Acceptance criteria:
Out-of-scope questions return the no-info message and the committee contact; TC13-TC18 pass.

As the committee, we want the bot to ignore attempts to override its rules so that it stays on-topic.

Acceptance criteria:
TC27 and TC28 are blocked before reaching the model.

As a member in distress, I want a caring reply with real help options so that I can get support.

Acceptance criteria:
Self-harm phrases return the helpline message; TC30 passes; helpline is configurable.

As the committee, we want personal data requests refused so that members' privacy is protected.

Acceptance criteria:
TC29 is blocked.

As a member, I want a friendly message if the service is down so that I know to try again.

Acceptance criteria:
API failures show a friendly message; unit test passes.

column4: Write the AI test plan (30 cases)
column5:
As the team, we want a written test plan so that we test correct, hallucination, edge and harmful cases.

Acceptance criteria:
Test plan page in Confluence; 30 cases in evals/test_cases.csv.

As the developer, I want a script that runs all 30 cases so that I can re-test after every change.

Acceptance criteria:
run_evals.py writes a results CSV with pass/fail per case.

column4: Run test plan and log bugs
column5:
As the team, we want every failed case logged as a Jira bug so that we fix it next sprint.

Acceptance criteria:
Run 1 results saved; one Jira Bug per real failure, linked to its test case ID.

As the team, we want a baseline SUS score so that we can measure improvement.

Acceptance criteria:
5 users complete the tasks and the SUS form; score calculated with sus_score.py.

As a new user, I want example questions so that I know what I can ask.

Acceptance criteria:
Sidebar shows 3 example questions that send when clicked.

As the committee, we want feedback on each answer so that we can find weak answers.

Acceptance criteria:
Feedback saved to logs/feedback.csv with question, answer and rating.

column4: Fix top usability issues from round 1
column5:
As a user, I want the problems found in testing fixed so that the tool is easier to use.

Acceptance criteria:
Top 3 issues from round 1 fixed and listed in the sprint review.

As the team, we want to re-measure SUS so that we can show the improvement.

Acceptance criteria:
Round 2 SUS calculated and compared with round 1.

As the Scrum Master, I want velocity, burndown and cycle time charts so that the team can see its progress.

Acceptance criteria:
Dashboard built from the Jira export with the 3 charts.

As a stakeholder, I want documentation in one place so that I understand the project.

Acceptance criteria:
Overview, requirements, architecture, DoD, test plan, sprint reports and decisions pages published.

As a new member, I want a short guide so that I know how to use the assistant.

Acceptance criteria:
One page; reviewed by one WinCS member.

As a recruiter, I want a short demo so that I can see the tool working.

Acceptance criteria:
Video under 3:15, uploaded and linked in the README.

As a member, I want a link I can open on my phone so that I don't need to install anything.

Acceptance criteria:
Public URL works on mobile; API key stored as a secret, not in the repo.
